correctness.rationale: The displayed 14-by-3 row matrix satisfies the adjacency eigen-equation with eigenvalue 2 and has orthonormal columns. An exact incidence-matrix computation gives second eigenvalue 2 with multiplicity 3, so Winter's definition makes this the canonical eigenpolytope. The vertex norms yield the two shells; antipodal outer axis vertices force the unique minimum-enclosing sphere. Twelve explicit signed two-coordinate inequalities are all supporting facets, and Euler's formula shows completeness. Their equal support and normal norm give the exact inradius, while opposite facet pairs force the unique incenter.

value.rationale: Winter singles out the rhombic dodecahedron as the only known spectral polytope outside vertex transitivity and explicitly asks what characterizes such exceptions. The exact canonical metric profile supplies a concrete geometric signature of that exception: it is fully tangential and edge-equilateral, yet its two graph-vertex orbits occupy two different radius shells and only one orbit controls the minimum enclosing sphere. This is more informative than a coordinate rescaling alone and directly complements the symmetry discussion in the primary source.
